# Adult health questions we saved

Answers from a health insurer's member website, saved for reference.

## I have been throwing up and feel dizzy, should I see a doctor?

Most stomach bugs pass in a day or two. Rest, sip fluids, and eat bland food when you can. See a doctor if you are worried or if you are getting worse instead of better.

## Can I take two medicines at once?

Some medicines should not be combined. Read the label of each one and ask your pharmacist if you are not sure whether two of them go together.

## How can I tell the flu from a cold?

Colds are milder and build slowly; flu comes on suddenly and feels worse. Either way, rest and fluids help, and a doctor can test for flu.

## How do I know if my sprain is serious?

A mild sprain improves in a few days. See a doctor if the pain is severe, if the joint looks out of shape, or if it is not getting better.

## What should I keep in a first aid kit?

Bandages in several sizes, gauze pads, medical tape, antiseptic wipes, tweezers, scissors, a thermometer, disposable gloves, and any prescribed medicines. Check it twice a year and replace anything that has expired.

## How much water should I drink a day?

Needs differ with body size, activity and the weather. A pale yellow urine color is a simple sign that you are drinking enough.

## Should I use ice or heat on an injury?

Ice is usually used first for swelling, and heat later for stiffness, but it depends on the injury. Ask your doctor or a physical therapist what is right for yours.
